title: Interpreting the value of the `INFO` attribute in the `logging` module as a log level constant
question: What is the output if you replace the `logging.INFO` attribute value with its name?
explanation: 1) Use `import logging` to make the `logging` module available. 2) Read the value of the `INFO` attribute from ``logging.INFO``. 3) Store that level value in `level`. 4) Call `getLevelName` to retrieve the name of that level (`INFO`) and print it.
reading_goal: Distinguish between the module name to the left of the dot and the attribute name to the right of the dot in `logging.INFO`, and read the value of the constant at the current level.
project_context: This connects to the process of setting logging levels—such as `basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)`—at the CLI entry point.
reading_goal_internal: `logging.INFO`에서 점 왼쪽 모듈과 점 오른쪽 속성 이름을 구분하고 현재 레벨 상수 값을 읽는다.

concept_explanation.what_it_is: Module attribute access is an expression that reads the value of a specific attribute from a module object obtained in the form `module.name`.
concept_explanation.how_to_read: `logging.INFO` In this context, `logging` is a module, and `INFO` is a level constant attribute defined within that module.
concept_explanation.key_point: The `INFO` constant can be passed as a configuration value such as the `level` argument of `basicConfig`.
concept_explanation.common_mistake: It’s easy to assume that `INFO` is a function and must therefore be called as `logging.INFO()`.

teaching_example.walkthrough: `WARNING` is an attribute of the `logging` module, and its name can be retrieved using `getLevelName`.

answer_explanation.step_by_step: 1) Use `import logging` to make the `logging` module available. 2) Read the value of the `INFO` attribute from ``logging.INFO``. 3) Store that level value in `level`. 4) Call `getLevelName` to retrieve the name of that level (`INFO`) and print it.
answer_explanation.why_correct: Since `logging.INFO` is an INFO-level constant, looking up its name returns `INFO`.

common_wrong_choice.why_wrong: DEBUG is another module attribute called `logging.DEBUG`.
common_wrong_choice.misread_step: Check the actual attribute name written to the right of the dot.

answer_explanation.takeaway: Accessing a module's attributes is interpreted as **identifying the module object → identifying the attribute name → reading the attribute value**.

title: Select one value from the DEBUG or INFO levels using the verbose condition
question: In this code, what is the name of the log level that is ultimately output when `verbose` is False?
code:
import logging
verbose = False
level = logging.DEBUG if verbose else logging.INFO
print(logging.getLevelName(level))
explanation: 1) The current value of `verbose` is `True`. 2) Check that the condition in the conditional expression is `True`. 3) Do not select the `INFO` following `else`; instead, select the preceding `logging.DEBUG` as the result. 4) The level name `DEBUG` is printed.
reading_goal: Reads the false branch of the conditional expression where INFO is selected when `verbose=False`.
project_context: `--verbose` It is linked to CLI logging settings that write detailed DEBUG logs when enabled and use the INFO level otherwise.
reading_goal_internal: verbose가 False일 때 조건 표현식의 else 값인 INFO가 선택되는 실행 순서를 읽는다.

concept_explanation.what_it_is: The conditional expression `A if condition else B` selects one of two values as the result of the expression based on the result of `condition`.
concept_explanation.how_to_read: First, check the condition "verbose" in the middle; if it is True, select the logging.DEBUG statement before it, and if it is False, select the logging.INFO statement after the "else" block.
concept_explanation.key_point: Since `verbose=True`, the DEBUG level is selected this time.
concept_explanation.common_mistake: It’s easy to assume that, when reading from left to right, both DEBUG and INFO are included in the evaluation results, or that INFO is always the default.

teaching_example.code:
debug_mode = True
label = "DEBUG" if debug_mode else "INFO"
print(label)
teaching_example.walkthrough: Since `debug_mode` is True, the string `DEBUG` at the beginning of the conditional expression is selected.

answer_explanation.step_by_step: 1) `verbose` is False. 2) The conditional expression evaluates `verbose` first. 3) Since it is False, it skips the `logging.DEBUG` on the left and selects `logging.INFO` after `else`. 4) The `level` variable is set to the INFO level, and the last line prints the name ``INFO``.
answer_explanation.why_correct: This is because a conditional expression uses the value following ``else`` as the result when the condition is `False`.

common_wrong_choice.why_wrong: DEBUG is the leading value selected when verbose is True. The current value is False.
common_wrong_choice.misread_step: This is a case where the first candidate in the conditional expression was interpreted as the result without first checking the condition value.

answer_explanation.takeaway: Read a conditional expression as **evaluate condition first → if True choose the front value / if False choose the value after `else` → only one selected value becomes the result**.

title: Reading the `action` keyword argument in an `add_argument` call
question: Because of `action='store_true'`, what value is passed to the `action` parameter?
explanation: 1) Check the call target add_argument. 2) The string --verbose is passed as the first argument. 3) The keyword argument action on the left is a parameter name. 4) The string store_true on the right is passed to that action parameter.
reading_goal: In `action='store_true'`, the left side represents the name of the parameter to be received, and the string on the right represents the actual value being passed.
project_context: This ties into the process of registering on/off options—such as --verbose and --force—in argparse for the CLI.
reading_goal_internal: `action='store_true'`에서 왼쪽은 받을 매개변수 이름이고 오른쪽 문자열은 실제 전달값이라는 구조를 읽는다.

concept_explanation.what_it_is: A keyword argument is a `name=value` format that directly specifies the name of a parameter to be received in a function or method call.
concept_explanation.how_to_read: Do not read `action='store_true'` as a standard assignment statement; instead, interpret it as passing a string to the `action` parameter within the `add_argument` call.
concept_explanation.key_point: In argparse, this action requests Boolean-flag behavior: True when the option is present and False when it is absent.
concept_explanation.common_mistake: It is easy to mistake `store_true` for the Boolean value `True` itself or for the name of a separate variable.

teaching_example.walkthrough: The ``mode='safe'`` function directly passes the string "safe" to the `mode` parameter.

answer_explanation.step_by_step: 1) Check the call target add_argument. 2) The string --verbose is passed as the first argument. 3) The keyword argument action on the left is a parameter name. 4) The string store_true on the right is passed to that action parameter.
answer_explanation.why_correct: The actual value passed to the keyword argument is the string `store_true` on the right side of the equals sign.

common_wrong_choice.why_wrong: Although `argparse` interprets the `store_true` action, the flag result may be `True`; however, the value passed to the `action` parameter at the time of the call is the string `store_true`.
common_wrong_choice.misread_step: It distinguishes between the values passed at the time of a call and the resulting behavior produced later.

answer_explanation.takeaway: Keyword arguments are read as **check parameter name → evaluate value on the right → pass it to the corresponding parameter**.

title: Select one value—DEBUG or INFO—using the "verbose" condition
question: What is the name of the log level that is ultimately output when `verbose` is set to True?
code:
import logging
verbose = True
level = logging.DEBUG if verbose else logging.INFO
print(logging.getLevelName(level))
explanation: 1) The current value of `verbose` is `True`. 2) The conditional expression evaluates the `verbose` part in the middle first. 3) Since the condition is `True`, the `logging.DEBUG` statement on the left is selected. 4) When the name of that level is looked up, `DEBUG` is printed.
reading_goal: In `A if condition else B`, the flow is to first evaluate the verbose expression in the middle and then select only the log level on one side that represents the actual result.
project_context: -- This is linked to the CLI configuration process that enables more detailed DEBUG logs when `--verbose` is present.
reading_goal_internal: `A if condition else B`에서 가운데 verbose를 먼저 평가하고 실제 결과가 되는 한쪽 로그 레벨만 선택하는 흐름을 읽는다.

concept_explanation.what_it_is: A conditional expression takes the form `A if condition else B` and returns one of two possible values based on the condition.
concept_explanation.how_to_read: First, evaluate the condition in the middle; if it is True, select the value before the `if` statement; if it is False, select the value after the `else` statement.
concept_explanation.key_point: Since `verbose` is set to `True`, `logging.DEBUG` is selected.
concept_explanation.common_mistake: Reading from left to right, it’s easy to assume that both DEBUG and INFO are executed or appear together in the output.

teaching_example.code:
verbose = False
level = "DEBUG" if verbose else "INFO"
print(level)
teaching_example.walkthrough: Since the condition is False, the single "INFO" string following the `else` statement is the result.

answer_explanation.step_by_step: 1) The current value of `verbose` is `True`. 2) The conditional expression evaluates the `verbose` part in the middle first. 3) Since the condition is `True`, the `logging.DEBUG` statement on the left is selected. 4) When the name of that level is looked up, `DEBUG` is printed.
answer_explanation.why_correct: Since the condition is True, the `logging.DEBUG` before the `if` statement becomes the result of the expression.

common_wrong_choice.why_wrong: INFO is the value selected by the `else` branch when `verbose` is set to `False`.
common_wrong_choice.misread_step: First, determine the condition value, then check which candidate is selected.

answer_explanation.takeaway: Conditional expressions are read in the following order: **evaluate the condition → select one of the values → return the selected value**.

title: Replace the logging level constant with a named string via a function call
question: What is the return string of `logging.getLevelName(logging.INFO)`?
explanation: 1) Read the value of the `logging.INFO` attribute. 2) Pass that value as a positional argument to `getLevelName`. 3) The function returns the name string for that log level. 4) The return value `INFO` is stored in `level_name` and printed.
reading_goal: Read the flow where the `logging.INFO` value is passed as a function argument and the `getLevelName` call returns the `INFO` string.
project_context: In larger-scale CLI environments, this ties into the process of managing operational and debugging messages by distinguishing log severity levels beyond simple output.
reading_goal_internal: logging.INFO 값을 함수 인자로 전달하고 getLevelName 호출이 INFO 문자열을 반환하는 흐름을 읽는다.

concept_explanation.what_it_is: A function call evaluates the arguments inside the parentheses, passes them to the called function, and produces a return value.
concept_explanation.how_to_read: First, read the value of the argument `logging.INFO`, then check the result of the outer `getLevelName` call.
concept_explanation.key_point: A key feature that distinguishes `logging` from a simple `print` is its ability to handle level information such as `DEBUG`, `INFO`, and `WARNING`.
concept_explanation.common_mistake: It is easy to assume that the function name `getLevelName` itself is printed, or that the `INFO` attribute value is always an object with the string value `INFO`.

teaching_example.walkthrough: If a level value is passed as an argument, the call returns the string "WARNING," which is the name of that level.

answer_explanation.step_by_step: 1) Read the value of the `logging.INFO` attribute. 2) Pass that value as a positional argument to `getLevelName`. 3) The function returns the name string for that log level. 4) The return value `INFO` is stored in `level_name` and printed.
answer_explanation.why_correct: `getLevelName` returns the name string `INFO`, which corresponds to the `INFO` level value.

common_wrong_choice.why_wrong: DEBUG is a different log level corresponding to `logging.DEBUG`.
common_wrong_choice.misread_step: Check whether the argument actually passed to the function is INFO or DEBUG.

answer_explanation.takeaway: A function call is described as **evaluating arguments → calling the function → checking the return value**.

title: Passing the current path value as the second argument to the progress log call
question: What is the actual value passed as the second argument in the call?
code:
def record(template, value):
    return template % value

input_path = "data.json"
message = record("읽는 중: %s", input_path)
print(message)
explanation: 1) Before the call, `input_path` points to the string `data.json`. 2) The first argument of the `record` call is a format string. 3) Evaluating the `input_path` expression in the second position yields `data.json`. 4) That string is passed to the `value` parameter to create a progress message.
reading_goal: Read the structure where the second expression, `input_path`, inside the call parentheses is evaluated, and its current string value is passed to the second parameter.
project_context: This is linked to a progress log that records the processing steps and target path, similar to `logging.info('Reading: %s', input_path)`.
reading_goal_internal: 호출 괄호 안 두 번째 표현식 input_path가 평가되어 그 현재 문자열 값이 두 번째 매개변수에 전달되는 구조를 읽는다.

concept_explanation.what_it_is: Positional arguments are values passed to parameters in the order they appear within the call parentheses, without being named.
concept_explanation.how_to_read: Separate the first format string from the second input_path expression using commas, and evaluate the current value of input_path.
concept_explanation.key_point: The actual value passed as the second argument is the string `data.json`.
concept_explanation.common_mistake: It is easy to assume that the character string `input_path` itself is passed to the function.

teaching_example.code:
def record(template, value):
    return template % value
path = "input.csv"
print(record("읽기: %s", path))
teaching_example.walkthrough: The current string `input.csv`, which is the second positional argument `path`, is passed as the `value` parameter.

answer_explanation.step_by_step: 1) Before the call, `input_path` points to the string `data.json`. 2) The first argument of the `record` call is a format string. 3) Evaluating the `input_path` expression in the second position yields `data.json`. 4) That string is passed to the `value` parameter to create a progress message.
answer_explanation.why_correct: Positional arguments pass the current value of the expression, not the variable name itself.

common_wrong_choice.why_wrong: `input_path` without quotation marks is a variable reference, not a string literal.
common_wrong_choice.misread_step: Distinguish between name references and string literals.

answer_explanation.takeaway: Position arguments are read in the following order: **expression evaluation → determination of current value → order of writing**.

title: Separating developer debug logs from user error messages
question: `logging.debug("input_path=%s", input_path)` Which of the following is the most appropriate role for the line?
choices: The `input_path` value is logged in the debug log so that developers can verify it.
It displays the entire contents of the input file on the screen to the user.
Automatically generates the `input_path` string as an actual file
Ignore the SystemExit below and continue execution
answer: The `input_path` value is logged in the debug log so that developers can verify it.
explanation: The `input_path` variable stores the string ``data/input.json``. The ``logging.debug(...)`` on the next line passes that value as data to the debug log. Since ``file_exists`` is False, the `if` branch is executed, and a separate exit message—``입력 파일이 없습니다``—is displayed to the user. The problematic `target` line is a function call that passes the internal value ``input_path`` to the debug log, so the first option is correct. A common source of confusion: The `debug` call that displays the entire contents of the input file to the user (`input_path`) merely passes the value `` itself to the debug log; it does not read the file contents or guarantee that they are displayed on the user’s screen. Point of Misinterpretation: Do not confuse the arguments of ``logging.debug`` with the user messages at ``raise SystemExit`` as coming from the same output path. Debug logs are for internal diagnostics, while user error messages are for user guidance; they serve distinct purposes.
reading_goal: Recognize that a `logging.debug` call is a function call that logs internal diagnostic values, and distinguish it from user message handling.
project_context: Operational tools often log developer diagnostic information separately from error messages that users need to understand.
reading_goal_internal: logging.debug 호출이 내부 진단값을 로그로 전달하는 함수 호출임을 읽고 사용자 메시지 처리와 구분한다.

concept_explanation.what_it_is: `logging.debug(...)` is a function call that generates debug-level logs so that developers can track the program’s internal state.
concept_explanation.how_to_read: The first value in parentheses is the log format, and the value that follows is the actual data to be filled into that format. The purpose of this call is to record diagnostic information rather than to return a value and perform a calculation.
concept_explanation.key_point: Developer logs and user messages serve different purposes. Internal paths and states can be recorded in debug logs, while users can be provided with short, easy-to-understand messages.
concept_explanation.common_mistake: Just because a value is logged does not mean it will be displayed exactly as is on every user’s screen. Whether the log is output depends on the logging settings.

teaching_example.walkthrough: The `logging.debug` call passes the `user_id` value to the diagnostic log. It is not a statement that stores or returns the value 17 in another variable.

answer_explanation.step_by_step: The `input_path` variable stores the string ``data/input.json``. The ``logging.debug(...)`` on the next line passes that value as data to the debug log. Since ``file_exists`` is False, the `if` branch is executed, and the user is shown a separate exit message: ``입력 파일이 없습니다``.
answer_explanation.why_correct: Since the target line in the problem is a function call that passes the internal value ``input_path`` to the debug log, the first option is correct.

common_wrong_choice.choice: It displays the entire contents of the input file on the screen to the user.
common_wrong_choice.why_wrong: A `debug` call simply passes the `input_path` value itself to the diagnostic log; it does not read the file’s contents or guarantee that the user will see it on the screen.
common_wrong_choice.misread_step: `logging.debug` Do not combine the arguments of ``raise SystemExit`` with the user message from `` into the same output path.

answer_explanation.takeaway: Distinguish the roles: debug logs are for internal diagnostics, while user error messages are for guiding the user.

title: Selecting the log level using the `verbose` value
question: `level = logging.DEBUG if verbose else logging.INFO` What is the role of "verbose CLI"?
code:
import logging

verbose = False
level = logging.DEBUG if verbose else logging.INFO
print(level == logging.INFO)
choices: Select "DEBUG" when verbose mode is on, and "INFO" when it is off to change the log detail level.
If `verbose` is turned off, logging itself is disabled.
logging parses command-line arguments instead of argparse
answer: Select "DEBUG" when verbose mode is on, and "INFO" when it is off to change the log detail level.
explanation: 1) Check the verbose status. 2) If True, select logging.DEBUG; if False, select logging.INFO. 3) The selected level determines the level of detail for subsequent logging settings. This explanation interprets the Python target of this card—which states that selecting DEBUG when `verbose` is on and INFO when it is off changes the log detail level—by linking it to legacy/domain objectives. Common Misconception: “Turning off verbose disables logging entirely.” This option focuses only on specific syntax or context within the code and misses the card’s core meaning. Point of misinterpretation: If you only check whether `True` is output when `verbose=False`, you miss the connection between argparse, verbose, and logging. The verbose CLI should be interpreted as **option state → log level selection → logging configuration**.
reading_goal: Read the CLI flow where the `verbose` option’s state is linked to the selection of a logging level.
project_context: This is the context for reading code that selects either the DEBUG or INFO log level based on the ``--verbose`` option in the CLI.
reading_goal_internal: verbose 옵션의 상태가 logging 레벨 선택으로 연결되는 CLI 흐름을 읽는다.

concept_explanation.what_it_is: A conditional expression is an expression that selects one value in the form `value_if_true if condition else value_if_false`.
concept_explanation.how_to_read: First, check the condition in the middle. If the condition is True, select the value before `if`; if False, select the value after `else`.
concept_explanation.key_point: The result of a conditional expression is not simply True or False, but a value that selects the actual logging level based on the CLI’s verbose status.
concept_explanation.common_mistake: If you only check whether `True` is printed when `verbose=False`, you’ll miss the purpose of linking argparse, `verbose`, and logging.

teaching_example.code:
compact = True
spacing = 8 if compact else 16
print(spacing)
teaching_example.walkthrough: Since `compact` is True, the 8 before the `if` statement is selected and stored in `spacing`.

answer_explanation.step_by_step: 1) Check the `verbose` status. 2) If True, select `logging.DEBUG`; if False, select `logging.INFO`. 3) The selected level determines the level of detail for subsequent logging settings.
answer_explanation.why_correct: This is an explanation that interprets the Python target of this card—which states that you can change the log detail level by selecting "DEBUG" when "verbose" is enabled and "INFO" when it is disabled—in relation to legacy and domain objectives.

common_wrong_choice.choice: If `verbose` is turned off, logging itself is disabled.
common_wrong_choice.why_wrong: This option focuses only on certain aspects of the code’s syntax or context and misses the core meaning of the card.
common_wrong_choice.misread_step: If you only check whether `True` is printed when `verbose=False`, you’ll miss the purpose of linking argparse, `verbose`, and logging.

answer_explanation.takeaway: "Verbose CLI" should be read as **option status → log level selection → logging configuration**.

target_statement: level = logging.DEBUG if verbose else logging.INFO
